Sign Up

to submit an obituary

For information on submitting an obituary, please contact Reading Eagle by phone at 610-371-5018, or email at obituaries@readingeagle.com or fax at 610-371-5193.

Most obituaries published in the Reading Eagle are submitted through funeral homes and cremation services, but we will accept submissions from families. Obituaries can be emailed to obituaries@readingeagle.com.

In addition to the text of the obituary, any photographs that you wish to include can be attached to this email. Please put the text of the obituary in a Word document, a Google document or in the body of the email. The Reading Eagle also requires a way to verify the death, so please include either the phone number of the funeral home or cremation service that is in charge of the deceased's care or a photo of his/her death certificate. We also request that your full name, phone number and address are all included in this email.

All payments by families must be made with a credit card. We will send a proof of the completed obituary before we require payment. The obituary cannot run, however, until we receive payment in full.

Obituaries can be submitted for any future date, but they must be received no later than 3:00 p.m. the day prior to its running for it to be published.

Please call the obituary desk, at 610-371-5018, for information on pricing.

    Penn State football: Former Nazareth star Peyton Falzone switches positions

    Share this:

    • Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook
    • Share on X (Opens in new window) X
    • Click to share a free article with a friend

    By Rich Scarcella | rscarcella@readingeagle.com | Reading Eagle
    PUBLISHED: August 13, 2026 at 1:58 PM EDT | UPDATED: August 14, 2026 at 7:52 AM EDT
    Getting your Trinity Audio player ready...
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 1:53
    Instaread

    Former Nazareth High School star Peyton Falzone has been moved from quarterback to tight end at Penn State, Nittany Lions coach Matt Campbell confirmed Thursday.

    The 6-5, 216-pound Falzone was rated a four-star prospect by ESPN and On3 and a three-star prospect by 247Sports. He was ranked as high as the No. 8 quarterback in the country in the Class of 2026 and as low as No. 22.

    He initially committed to Penn State, flipped to Auburn and flipped back to the Nittany Lions.

    “Peyton made some really special plays (Wednesday) with the ball in his hands,” Campbell said. “Peyton has a 38-inch vertical jump and ran under a 4.5 40. You’re like, ‘Man, this guy has so much athleticism. Can he help our football team more somehow, some way?’

    “I give him a lot of credit because he did what was best for the team. We left that quarterback piece open. What was best for the team and for him right now was to see what he could do (at tight end). I’m proud of him. It’s only been two days. It’ll be a work in progress. We’re really excited about what he can do.”

    As a senior, he passed for 1,176 yards and 12 touchdowns and ran for 216 yards and six TDs before he suffered a season-ending injury. In his final three seasons at Nazareth, he passed for 5,840 yards and 55 touchdowns.

    At quarterback, Falzone was behind expected starter Rocco Becht and primary backup Alex Manske. Kase Evans, who’s from Lexington, Texas, was the other quarterback in Penn State’s latest recruiting class. Connor Barry and Jack Lambert are the other quarterbacks on the roster.

    Falzone joins a talented tight end room, which includes Ben Brahmer, Gabe Burkle, Andrew Rappleyea, Cooper Alexander, Finn Furmanek and Brian Kortovich. If he stays there, he’d be the only true freshman tight end.
